answer: The cost lands per head: 294 aliases need 294 records, each checked live against the issuer, so bulk forgery costs 294 times what one honest seat costs. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Entry needs deep sea research cruise participation log: cruises sailed with one institute across years of ocean surveys. The island is the bottleneck and the terrace is the receipt: a farm must clear both for each of its 294 aliases, the quartz trail is public, and one honest agent clears them once.
